supplementaryEvidence.supports: Discard may use owned Hand or Equipment and is chosen by the player. Both branches perform one pair before their stopping test. Voluntarily choosing discard requires two payable cards; the compulsory ending discard instead pays all remaining cards when fewer than two. Military-standard damaging tricks are Duel, FireAttack, BarbarianAssault and ArrowBarrage.

interpretations.basis: Primary ordering plus the explicit same-product clarification.
interpretations.implementation: Choose one first branch once in the actual Play phase. Draw two or privately select an entire two-card HE discard set, commit the real pair, drain native children, then test the current effective hand. No pre-test bypass and no fixed number of iterations. The initial voluntary discard is unavailable with fewer than two legally discardable cards. Mandatory later payments discard up to the remaining legal count, including zero or one.

interpretations.basis: Primary hand condition and same-product standard damaging-card list; interactions with card identity rules use the engine's native effective hand kind.
interpretations.implementation: Discard repeats while at least one Slash or damaging trick remains in hand; draw repeats while none remains. The four military-standard damaging tricks listed in the guide are examples of the current broad primary category: native UnexpectedAssault (出其不意) also qualifies because its ordinary-trick effect can cause damage. This additional-card classification is an engine-category inference, not a claimed character FAQ. Equipment presence is not part of the stop test. Optional view-as possibilities do not change a card's hand identity. Each comparison occurs after native movement, HP, skills, damage and rescue children. No actual draw or no legal discard terminates an otherwise impossible further payment rather than fabricating cards or looping forever.

interpretations.basis: Primary says this phase ending, and the later guide confirms separate actual extra Plays.
interpretations.implementation: The first real payment issues an immutable attributable obligation with the original skill instance, gameplay hash, actual turn and native Play instance. Only that same native PlayEnding can consume it once. The actual parent window freezes its phase identity before an earlier trigger can insert another Play. An inserted Play may create and consume its own separate opposite branch before the original ending resumes. No extra turn or extra Discard is introduced.

interpretations.rule: Source lifetime and native equipment effects
interpretations.basis: Issued effect continuation and the existing native card-movement contract; these edge cases are engine-rule inferences rather than a claimed current character FAQ.
interpretations.implementation: Losing the skill after a paid first branch preserves its exact later obligation and paid loop. Death drains the paid native subtree and stops new payments; a skipped or nonexistent phase ending never migrates an old obligation to another phase. Atomic HE discard records every selected physical entity before native SilverLion recovery, WoodenOx grain disposal and skill-source changes. Ongoing choices and movement tails remain on their owning ProgramSkillFrame and use typed native returns.

runtime.pendingOwnership: Original branch, exact Play key, frozen legal candidates, selected HE entities, required count, iteration, primary movement span and native side-effect tail are on ProgramSkillFrame.WangKuangRenxia. Collection init setters defensively copy into read-only collections. There is no mutable pending sidecar.
runtime.events: New events contain only scalars or immutable scalar records, including one discard-entity fact per actual entity. All rule facts use AdvanceEventRulesAndQueueFact. Private prompts use actual player snapshots and reveal no foreign hand identities.
runtime.contracts: Strict composition requires one original zero-input once-per-Play activation and its one mandatory issued own PlayEnding trigger. Issued candidates after source loss require the exact parent candidate cursor and an attributable paid obligation. Native movement, recovery, damage and dying observers accept only the exact paid receipt subtree.
